story_text:
The EEW Maker Kit spins like a high-end spinning wheel because it is one. But this one, you build yourself. As crafters, I know you understand the special pride that comes from making things with your own hands, and this kit brings that same magic to the tool itself.
Pair your own 3D-printed parts with this hardware kit to build an amazing eSpinner. I supply the high-quality core components, including the custom motor, steel spindle, circuit board, hardware, and open-source project files. By printing the chassis in your favorite colors and assembling it yourself, you create a professional-grade fiber tool that is uniquely yours.
More than just building a tool, backing this project means joining the journey. While the hardware foundation is solid, running this campaign gives us the chance to build a community together, share modifications, and watch the ecosystem grow. Whether you want to design new accessories, suggest refinements, or follow along as the story of this wheel develops, your input helps make the final product better for everyone.
If you don't have a 3D printer, I have you covered. I am setting up an Authorized Printer Network to connect you with a small group of trusted makers in the community who can print the parts for you.
Photo by Craftmehappy
## What’s in the Hardware Kit?
Every hardware kit comes packed with all the non-printable components required to bring your eSpinner to life.
- Electronics: A fully assembled main circuit board, brushless motor, display, speed controller, toggle switches, foot switch, and all necessary wiring harnesses.
- Mechanics: A precision-machined stainless steel spindle, front and back spindle bearings, and 10 bobbin bearings (enough for 5 bobbins).
- Hardware & Fasteners: Ceramic yarn guides, drive belts, tension string, springs, rubber feet, O-rings, and every screw needed to assemble your 3D-printed eSpinner.

## Spinning Performance
A custom-built wheel is only great if it actually performs. This kit features my most advanced eSpinner controller yet, a big step above even the EEW Fold. It actively monitors your motor, keeping your speed smooth whether you are spinning fine lace or bulky art yarn. In fact, art yarn now spins better than on any of my previous eSpinners thanks to the new ceramic guides and a completely redesigned flyer.
I want you to have complete control over how this machine feels so I added more software controls. You can adjust the soft start and soft stop ramps to your exact preference. I also built in a new tangle-detection feature that quickly stops the flyer if your yarn snags or something hits it.
Photo by Theresa Ehlers
## eSpinner Specifications
Since the chassis is 3D printed, the final weight and footprint will depend on the design and plastic you choose. Based on my standard open-source files, here is what you can expect:
- Bobbin Capacity: 8 oz (Bobbins are about the same size as the EEW 6.1)
- Speed Range: 200 to 1600 RPM at the flyer
- Assembled Weight: Approximately 3 lbs
- Dimensions: 4.7" W x 8.1" L x 7.7" H (120mm x 205mm x 195mm)
- Motor: Custom-wound TEC 3650 brushless motor
- Power: 12V 3A power supply (You must supply this - see the next section)
Photo by Vampy
## Power & Battery Options
To keep the base kit affordable, a power supply is not included by default. This gives you the freedom to choose the power solution that best fits your spinning setup:
Standard Wall Power: You can add a US-style wall adapter to your pledge as an add-on, or simply use your own standard 12V 3A power supply.
12V Battery: For a completely portable setup, the TalentCell 12V 6000mAh (USB-A) battery provides over 8 hours of typical spinning. I have already designed a free 3D-printable holder specifically for it. Any 12V battery outputting at least 2A with a 5.5x2.1mm (or 5.5x2.5mm) barrel connector will also work.
USB-C Power Banks: If you prefer using a more modern power bank, you just need one that supports USB-C with Power Delivery (PD) of 45W or more with a 12V output, like the INIU Power Bank Mini (which also has a free 3D-printable holder available). You will need to pair it with a standard USB-C to 12V 3A PD cable to connect it to the wheel.
## Assembly & Open Source
Building your own eSpinner shouldn't be intimidating. I rigorously beta-tested the build process with my Discord community to make sure it is straightforward and intuitive, utilizing more beta testers than I have ever had for any past project. There is no soldering, no complex wiring, and no coding required. I provide a detailed Assembly Guide showing exactly how the hardware plugs, snaps, and screws into your printed chassis.
Because the 3D files are completely open-source, this machine evolves with you. I provide the standard STL files for quick and easy printing, allowing you to get started immediately by just picking your favorite colors. For those who want to dig deeper, I also include the original Autodesk Fusion files so you can modify the core design to fit your exact spinning style. Want a massive jumbo bobbin or a fun custom twist keeper? Go for it.
This open-source approach guarantees total repairability, empowering you to maintain, reprint, or upgrade individual components so the wheel lasts a lifetime. You aren’t just getting an eSpinner; you’re joining an active community of makers sharing their own custom upgrades.
This is a custom jumbo 16 oz bobbin (twice the normal capacity) and modified sliding hooks designed by beta tester Craftmehappy.
## No 3D Printer? No Problem
You do not need to own a 3D printer to build an EEW Maker Kit.
To make this accessible to everyone, I set up the Authorized Printer Network. These are small 3D-printing businesses from our community who understand the exact requirements of this project. I sent each of them a hand-built prototype of the hardware kit so they could physically test-fit their printed parts. This guarantees that the files they print work perfectly with the hardware before you place an order.
You simply pledge for the hardware kit here on Kickstarter, then order your printed chassis directly from one of these trusted makers in the colors you want. You should wait to order any prints until close to when I am shipping you the kit since it’s likely I’ll be continuing to improve the 3D parts based on feedback from this Kickstarter.
- Snortimer's Hub: United States
- Heart Forge: United States
- The Spinning Siren: United States
- Cat & Sparrow: Australia and New Zealand
- Dragons Dream 3D: United Kingdom
- Johannas 3D: European Union
Asking a friend, neighbor, or family member who owns a 3D printer is also a great route. Other options include checking your local library or using an on-demand service like Craftcloud (or RigidPrint in the UK). However, if you are not familiar with 3D printing settings, infill density, or working with different plastics like PLA/PETG, the simplest solution is ordering from the Authorized Printer Network. They know exactly what this wheel needs and will ensure your parts fit right out of the box.
The page with the 3D files for this project on Printables has some recommended settings for printing if you are looking for guidance.
## Reward Tiers & Add-Ons
Choose the pledge tier that best fits your timeline and how you want to participate in the campaign:
- EEW Maker Kit ($99): The standard reward for almost everyone. You get the complete hardware kit from the main manufacturing run, packed with the motor, circuit board, spindle, bearings, and fasteners. You provide the 3D-printed chassis either by printing it yourself using my free open-source files, or ordering the parts from the Authorized Printer Network. Ships via ocean freight to my warehouse with estimated delivery to you in August 2027.
- Early Access - EEW Maker Kit ($139): Want to start building as soon as possible and help pioneer the release? This tier reserves a hardware kit from a small, expedited batch flown directly by air freight to my warehouse instead of traveling by sea. Along with getting your kit roughly two months ahead of standard fulfillment (estimated June 2027), you’ll be among the first to build from the assembly guide, helping test and refine the documentation before the main batch arrives. This is limited to 40 backers. It is the exact same hardware kit, just delivered early.
- (Optional Add-On) 12V Power Supply ($12): To keep the base kit affordable, power supplies are not included by default. If you spin in North America and want an official wall adapter ready to plug into your kit, you can add this to your pledge. If you are outside North America or prefer cordless spinning, check the Power & Battery Options section above for easy recommendations to power your wheel with local adapters, 12V batteries, or USB-C power banks.
Photo by Craftmehappy
## Project Goals
I started Dreaming Robots to make fiber arts tools more accessible, and the EEW Maker Kit takes that mission even further. This project is built around five core principles:
- Community Innovation: An open platform that empowers the community to modify, improve, and share new features.
- Customization: The freedom to adapt colors, ergonomics, and accessories to fit your exact spinning style.
- Pride of Ownership: The unique satisfaction of building a high-performance tool from the ground up rather than buying it off the shelf.
- Affordability: Providing a high-quality eSpinner at a lower price point by focusing on the core hardware and letting you handle the assembly.
- Repairability: Ensuring your wheel lasts a lifetime by empowering you to easily maintain, reprint, or upgrade parts anytime.
## Documentation & Technical Deep Dives
A huge amount of development and testing is already finished. I believe in keeping my work transparent, so if you want to see my decision process, review technical details, or read the build instructions before backing, you can explore the documentation below.
- EEW Maker Kit – Assembly Guide
- EEW Maker Kit – User Manual
- EEW Maker Kit – Programming Guide
- EEW Maker Kit – Design Document
- EEW Maker Kit – Bill of Materials (BOM)
- EEW Maker Kit – Electronics Interfaces
- 3D Files and CAD Files (Printables)
These documents and files are not final. They will all be updated during and after this Kickstarter. One reason I am running this campaign is to give the community time to share their ideas with me so I can incorporate that feedback into the final project before I ship.
Photo by Craftmehappy
## Proven Track Record
If you are new to my projects, I have been designing and manufacturing Electric Eel Wheels for over 15 years. I have successfully fulfilled nine previous Kickstarter campaigns, including the EEW 6.0, EEW Nano, and the recent EEW Fold. I know exactly what it takes to manage large-scale manufacturing, quality control, and global shipping. When you back this project, you can trust that I have the experience to actually deliver your hardware.
Photo by Craftmehappy
## The Funding Goal
The hardware design is finished, the firmware is dialed in, and the 3D files are ready to print. Now, I need your help to fund the manufacturing run. None of these hardware kits have been manufactured yet or exist in inventory. All rewards will be newly produced specifically for this Kickstarter campaign.

risks: With nine successfully fulfilled Kickstarter campaigns behind me, I understand how to manage hardware production, supply chains, and freight logistics. The EEW Maker Kit design is complete, and pricing accounts for current tariffs. I am also leaving a dedicated window in the production schedule to incorporate any significant community improvements suggested during the campaign. While international manufacturing and ocean shipping can experience unexpected delays, the fulfillment timeline includes buffer room to handle them. Quality is my top priority. If a production defect occurs, I will delay shipment rather than deliver a compromised tool. As with all my previous campaigns, I will keep you informed with regular, honest updates.
